questions.prompt: A browser visits the API over `http://` for the first time and later comes back. Put the events in order.
steps: The browser repeats the request over HTTPS
The HTTPS response carries the `Strict-Transport-Security` header from `UseHsts`
On the next visit, the browser rewrites `http://` to `https://` before sending anything
questions.explanation: The redirect is the safety net for the first contact; the HSTS header, once seen, makes the browser skip plain HTTP entirely on later visits.

questions.prompt: Why is `UseHttpsRedirection` on its own not fully secure?
options: It only redirects `POST` requests
It disables TLS for the redirected request
The first request has already travelled over plain HTTP, so its URL, headers and part of a body could be intercepted
Browsers ignore `308` redirects
questions.explanation: The redirect itself is harmless, but the original request was sent over an insecure channel before the client was told to switch to HTTPS.

questions.prompt: HSTS is set with `MaxAge = 365 days`, and users visit every week. When does a browser stop enforcing HTTPS-only?
options: Effectively never, because each HTTPS response resets the countdown; to clear it you serve `max-age=0`
Exactly 365 days after the first visit
As soon as the server stops accepting HTTPS
When the browser is restarted
questions.explanation: `max-age` is a rolling window: every time the browser sees the header, the full 365 days start again. An HSTS header with `max-age=0` tells browsers to forget the policy.

questions.prompt: What is the risk of turning on `IncludeSubDomains` carelessly?
options: Subdomains stop receiving the HSTS header
It doubles the `max-age` for every subdomain
The main domain falls back to HTTP
Any subdomain that can't serve HTTPS, such as an old internal tool or a staging site without a valid cert, breaks for browsers that cached the policy
questions.explanation: With `includeSubDomains` the policy covers every subdomain, even ones not created yet, so those without working HTTPS become unreachable for affected browsers.

questions.prompt: Why does the template call `app.UseHsts()` only when the environment is **not** Development?
options: HSTS headers are not supported by Kestrel in Development
Once a browser caches HSTS for `localhost`, it refuses plain HTTP to `localhost` for the whole `MaxAge`, breaking other local HTTP projects
Development certificates already include HSTS
`UseHttpsRedirection` stops working when HSTS is on
questions.explanation: Local development uses a self-signed dev certificate, and an aggressive HSTS policy cached for `localhost` would affect every other local tool; keeping it production-only avoids that.

questions.prompt: The app runs behind Nginx, which terminates TLS and forwards plain HTTP to Kestrel. What can go wrong without `app.UseForwardedHeaders()` before `UseHttpsRedirection()`?
options: The app sees every request as HTTP and may keep redirecting requests that were already secure, causing a redirect loop
Nothing; Kestrel always knows the original scheme
Nginx stops sending the `Host` header
HSTS headers get sent over plain HTTP to the client
questions.explanation: The proxy sends the original scheme in `X-Forwarded-Proto`; only `UseForwardedHeaders()` makes `Request.Scheme`/`IsHttps` reflect it, so it must come before the redirect middleware.

source.section: 3. Your app must trust and read those forwarded headers
